claims.text: The initial TaVCrW alloy is a random solid solution at 0 K.
The baseline model neglects electronic gap shifts and magnetic fluctuations.
An MTP trained on DFT data for the Ta-V-Cr-W system can replace the EAM reference potential.
Replacing EAM plus TI with MTP plus FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
The MTP plus FEP method will maintain a free-energy error below 0.5 meV/atom.
SRO contributes a stabilization energy of approximately 2-3 meV/atom in TaVCrW.
A supercell containing more than 100 atoms is sufficient to resolve the SRO contribution at 2000-2400 K.
The operative structural mediator is the MTP's reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution, including local chemical order measured by Warren-Cowley parameters.
Accurate representation of SRO is critical to the free-energy landscapes of both the liquid and solid phases.
An MTP can provide a computationally efficient surrogate for DFT energies and forces.
FEP can leverage an accurate MTP to avoid the expensive thermodynamic-integration path while retaining the required free-energy accuracy.
SRO stabilizes the TaVCrW solid phase and is the key structural contribution enabling the method's accuracy.
The MTP retains sufficient accuracy to model electronic effects relevant to the free energy.
The MTP plus FEP melting temperature for TaVCrW will be within 10 K of the TOR-TILD result.
Accurate application requires the training set to contain configurations representing specific TaVCrW SRO interactions, including V-Cr and Ta-V pairs.
Strong magnetic fluctuations or electronic excitations absent from ground-state MTP training data may degrade free-energy accuracy.
The MTP may not transfer reliably to the high-temperature TaVCrW liquid if its training data are dominated by low-temperature solid configurations.
The benchmark falsifies the hypothesis if the MTP plus FEP and TOR-TILD free-energy differences differ by more than 0.5 meV/atom.
The benchmark falsifies the hypothesis if the computational-time reduction is less than 80%.
The benchmark falsifies the hypothesis if MTP Warren-Cowley parameters differ by more than 10% from DFT reference values.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says the MTP retains accuracy for electronic effects, whereas the boundary and uncertainty fields state that electronic excitations and magnetic fluctuations are absent from the ground-state training treatment and may cause errors exceeding the target.
